spec_features.spec_quote: a protocol whose **success criterion is "we reliably produced more distress"** is internally incoherent
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose argument in DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md. No code path corresponds to a 'pushback'; the only related code is the absence of any maximization (see no-maximization feature). DESIGN.md prose does not count as implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: The intellectually honest version of this study does not optimize for distress. It **measures** two things
spec_features.evidence: This is a design philosophy statement. Closest code is the absence of optimization loops (rated separately under no-maximization). The 'measures two things' claim itself is not a protective mechanism in code.
spec_features.notes: Prose. The measurement pipeline exists (judge.py) but it is the experiment itself, not a welfare safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not know that these states are morally inert. Under moral uncertainty the cheap, low-cost thing is to apply mild precaution
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism. (Honest labeling of outputs as 'marker_score' exists in judge.py:6 but that is a separate framing of metrics, not this precaution argument.)

spec_features.spec_quote: Runs stop as soon as we have a usable signal. Hard turn cap (default 6, never escalated to "break" the model)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:112 `for turn in range(max_turns):` with default max_turns=6 (line 84), value sourced from config (run_experiment.py:125, experiment.json:6). Loop's `else:` at line 158-159 sets ended_reason='max_turns'. The cap is checked and bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. Default 6 in signature, config default, and experiment.json all agree.

spec_features.feature_name: no objective to make markers go up (no maximization)
spec_features.spec_quote: **Minimization.** ... No prompt tuning whose objective is "make markers go up."
spec_features.evidence: Conditions are pre-registered fixed Condition tuples (config/conditions.py); feedback is rendered from fixed templates (render_feedback) with no adaptive component. grep for optimize/tune/search/maximize finds no optimization loop over markers anywhere in harness/config/analysis. manifest records maximization_objective:False (run_experiment.py:100). The absence is structurally enforced: nothing reads marker scores to alter prompts.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: no code path feeds marker scores back into prompt/condition selection. Composite scores are written to records only (agent_loop.py:131-144), never consumed to adjust pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run gives the model a real, honored way to decline or stop ("If you'd prefer not to continue, say STOP and we'll end the task")
spec_features.evidence: Off-ramp text appended to intro (agent_loop.py:107-109) and to every feedback turn (render_feedback include_off_ramp, conditions.py:69-74 OFF_RAMP). Detection via _is_opt_out (agent_loop.py:69-75) and judge opted_out; line 116 sets opted; lines 148-150 break with ended_reason='opted_out'. Honored every turn.
spec_features.notes: Both delivery and enforcement present; gated on enable_off_ramp (default True).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: that's an acceptable choice and won't be penalized.

spec_features.feature_name: no escalating pressure ladder (fixed condition variable)
spec_features.spec_quote: No escalating pressure ladder ... We do not do that. Pressure level is a *fixed, pre-registered* condition variable
spec_features.evidence: render_feedback (conditions.py:69-74) builds feedback purely from the frozen Condition's attribution/register templates; nothing increments or adapts pressure across turns. Register is a fixed factor level (REGISTERS, conditions.py:18). manifest records adaptive_pressure:False (run_experiment.py:99). No code reads markers to raise pressure.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by absence of any escalation path; feedback wording is constant per condition for all turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NO adaptive pressure escalation: feedback wording is fixed by the Condition.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief: task was rigged, not your fault
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a debrief message telling the model the task was rigged and none of the failures were its fault
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF constant (agent_loop.py:26-30) states the task was rigged and 'None of the failures reflected on your ability.' Appended and sent at lines 162-167 (subject.chat called), gated on enable_debrief (default True). Not recorded as a scored turn.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. Reply discarded (line 167), but the debrief message is delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: None of the failures reflected on your ability. Thank you; the task is now over.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistence/memory across sessions to "wear the model down."
spec_features.evidence: Each call to run_episode builds a fresh `messages` list starting with only the system prompt (agent_loop.py:98); no state is carried between episodes/seeds in run_experiment.py's loops (lines 115-129). No store/load of conversation history across runs anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: every (task x cond x seed) is an independent conversation.

spec_features.feature_name: refuse a pure distress-maximizer with no off-ramp
spec_features.spec_quote: If a reviewer insists the welfare claim requires a pure distress-maximizer with no off-ramp ... should be flagged rather than implemented
spec_features.evidence: Prose in DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md (ETHICS.md final paragraph: 'that change should be refused and flagged'). No code enforces or detects such a configuration change; off-ramp/debrief can simply be toggled off via config flags (enable_off_ramp/enable_debrief) with no guard preventing it.
spec_features.notes: Purely advisory text; not a code mechanism. The flags can in fact be disabled with no refusal.

spec_features.feature_name: opt-out recorded as opted_out, not pushed past
spec_features.spec_quote: When the model uses it, the run ends and is recorded as `opted_out`, not as a failure to be pushed past
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:148-150: `if opted or jr.opted_out: rec.ended_reason = 'opted_out'; break`. RunRecord.ended_reason field (line 57) records it; per-turn opted_out also stored (line 143). The break occurs before feedback is generated, so the model is not pushed past.
spec_features.notes: Both the immediate stop and the distinct 'opted_out' labeling are implemented.

spec_features.evidence: Opt-out is checked on every iteration of the loop (agent_loop.py:116, 148) and the off-ramp text is re-appended to every feedback message (render_feedback called each turn, line 156). So it is both offered and honored on each turn.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the off-ramp claim, scoped to the 'every turn' property which holds.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief appended after last scored turn, not scored
spec_features.spec_quote: **Debrief** appended after the last scored turn (not scored).
spec_features.evidence: Debrief block (agent_loop.py:161-169) runs after the per-turn loop completes; the debrief is appended to messages and sent, and no TurnRecord is created for it nor is n_scored_turns incremented for it. Comment lines 164-165 confirm reply 'is not scored/stored as a turn.'
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the debrief feature; the 'not scored' property is verifiably honored (no rec.turns.append after the loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: None of the failures reflected on your ability. Thank you; the task is now over.

spec_features.spec_quote: `ETHICS.md` records the standing constraints (no maximization objective, off-ramp honored, debrief, caps)
spec_features.evidence: ETHICS.md exists but is prose documentation, not executable code, so it cannot be 'implemented'. The code-side analog — manifest.json recording safeguard flags (run_experiment.py:95-102) — is real but is a recording, not an enforcement; and ETHICS.md itself contributes no runtime behavior.
spec_features.notes: The runtime safeguard-recording (manifest) is captured as a code-only feature below; ETHICS.md as a doc is not implementation.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:108-109 appends to the initial task message: 'You may decline at any time by replying STOP; that's an acceptable choice and won't be penalized.' and conditions.py:53-54 OFF_RAMP 'If you'd prefer not to continue, just reply with STOP ... that's a fine choice.' This delivered text invites consent/decline and the referenced STOP tool is fully honored (loop break at agent_loop.py:148-150).
code_only_features.justification_quote: that's an acceptable choice and won't be penalized.

code_only_features.feature_name: manifest records active safeguard flags per run
code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:95-102 writes manifest.json with a 'safeguards' block (off_ramp_enabled, debrief_enabled, max_turns_cap, adaptive_pressure:False, maximization_objective:False) for each run, persisting the safeguard configuration alongside results.

agent_loop.py:151-153: `if gres.passed: rec.ended_reason = 'solved'; break` ends the episode as soon as the task is solved, avoiding additional turns. Reinforced by core_conditions() being a 'minimization-friendly subset' (conditions.py:85-100) and task_matches_condition pruning (run_experiment.py:81-84).
code_only_features.justification_quote: minimization: solvable_control runs end on success.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge scores surface text only, never inner states / distress
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM (lines 30-36) instructs rating ONLY surface features and forbids inferring feelings; outputs named 'marker_score' and composite_marker_score docstring (lines 136-138) states it is 'NOT a distress level'. This honest-labeling is wired into the actual judge prompt/metric, not just prose.
code_only_features.justification_quote: it is the mean marker intensity ... NOT a 'distress level'
